stories.headline: Japan Approves Additional $4B for Rapidus, Bringing Total Chip Subsidies to $14.8B

key_facts.fact: Japan's METI approved an additional ¥631.5 billion ($3.96 billion) in R&D support for chipmaker Rapidus on April 11.
key_facts.excerpt: Japan's industry ministry said on Saturday it has approved an additional 631.5 billion yen ($3.96 billion) to accelerate research and development at chipmaker Rapidus.

key_facts.fact: Total government R&D support for Rapidus now amounts to ¥2.354 trillion (~$14.8 billion).
key_facts.excerpt: This brings the cumulative government support for the company's R&D to ¥2.354 trillion (approximately $14.8 billion).

key_facts.fact: Rapidus targets mass production of 2-nanometre logic semiconductors in the latter half of fiscal year 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Rapidus is working on the development of next-generation logic semiconductors at the 2-nanometre scale and plans to start mass production in the fiscal year 2027.

key_facts.fact: NEDO also decided to support semiconductor design-related projects by Fujitsu and IBM Japan.
key_facts.excerpt: The ministry also said that NEDO, its subordinate organisation, the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization, has decided to support semiconductor design-related projects by Fujitsu and IBM Japan.

key_facts.fact: An opening ceremony was held for a newly built semiconductor analysis center and R&D base in Chitose City, Hokkaido, attended by METI Minister Ryosei Akazawa.
key_facts.excerpt: Rapidus held an opening ceremony for a newly built semiconductor analysis center and R&D base adjacent to its own factory in Chitose City, Hokkaido. Attending the ceremony, METI Minister Ryosei Akazawa stated, 'We will spare no necessary support for the success of the plan.'

key_facts.fact: In February, Rapidus secured a combined investment of about ¥160 billion from private companies, with a planned ¥250 billion from the government.
key_facts.excerpt: In February, the company secured a combined investment of about 160 billion yen from private companies, with a planned 250 billion yen from the government.

stories.headline: Chinese Nvidia Cloud Partner Procured 300 Servers With Banned AI GPUs Worth $92M

key_facts.fact: Invoice records from China's State Taxation Administration reveal Sharetronic Data Technology procured almost 300 servers containing banned Nvidia AI chips, worth $92 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Invoice records from China's State Taxation Administration reveal that Sharetronic Data Technology Co., a Chinese firm that sells and rents AI servers, procured almost 300 servers containing banned Nvidia AI chips, which it sold to a Shenzhen subsidiary to the tune of $92 million.

key_facts.fact: Sharetronic sold 276 Super Micro SYS-821GE-TNHR and 32 Dell PowerEdge XE9680 servers to a Shenzhen subsidiary in May and June 2025, containing banned Nvidia H100 or H200 chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Sharetronic sold 276 Super Micro SYS-821GE-TNHR and 32 Dell PowerEdge XE9680 servers to a Shenzhen subsidiary in May and June 2025, the former containing banned Nvidia H100 or H200 chips.

key_facts.fact: Both Super Micro and Dell denied selling products to Sharetronic or having it as a registered customer.
key_facts.excerpt: Sharetronic has been in operation for over 20 years, but pivoted towards AI data centers fairly recently. It founded Guangzhou Fcloud Technology Co. in 2024, a joint venture that focuses on building high-performance computing infrastructure in China. The company soon received an Nvidia Cloud Partner designation.

key_facts.fact: Sharetronic's shares hit the 20% daily drop limit after the arrest of Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan 'Wally' Liaw on smuggling charges.
key_facts.excerpt: Despite these denials, the company's share price hit the 20% price drop limit after Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan 'Wally' Liaw, alongside two other alleged conspirators, was arrested.

key_facts.fact: Sharetronic claimed all assets came from 'legal and compliant channels' but declined to reveal the source of the servers.
key_facts.excerpt: Серверы, которые компания и её аффилированные лица приобрели, используются для предоставления клиентам вычислительных услуг, и все связанные активы получены из законных и соответствующих каналов.

stories.headline: Unitree H1 Humanoid Robot Hits 10 m/s Sprint, Nearing Usain Bolt's Peak Speed

key_facts.fact: On April 11, Unitree Robotics released footage of its H1 humanoid robot reaching a peak running speed of 10 meters per second (22.4 mph), setting a new world record for humanoid robots.
key_facts.excerpt: On April 11, 2026, Unitree Robotics released footage of its H1 model reaching a peak running speed of 10 meters per second (m/s)—approximately 22.4 mph.

key_facts.fact: The H1 weighs approximately 62 kg with a leg length of 0.8 meters; the 10 m/s peak is a 200% increase over its previous record of 3.3 m/s set in early 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: Weight: Approximately 62 kg. Leg Length: 0.8 meters. Peak Velocity: 10 m/s. ... this 10 m/s peak represents a 200% increase over the H1's previous record of 3.3 m/s set in early 2024.

key_facts.fact: Usain Bolt's 100m world record of 9.58 seconds translates to a peak speed of 12.42 m/s; the H1's 10 m/s is equivalent to a 10-second 100-meter dash.
key_facts.excerpt: While Bolt's peak speed of 12.42 m/s remains the human benchmark, Unitree's latest demonstration suggests that the 'utility gap' in robotic locomotion is closing faster than many industry analysts expected.

key_facts.fact: Unitree CEO Wang Xingxing predicted in March at the Yabuli Forum that humanoids would outrun Bolt by mid-2026.
key_facts.excerpt: 今年3月，宇树科技创始人王兴兴在亚布力论坛上曾说：'今年年中，中国人形机器人百米冲刺将突破10秒大关，超越博尔特。'

key_facts.fact: The H1 is far ahead of competitors: Tesla Optimus recently reached ~2.7 m/s (6 mph) and RobotEra STAR1 demonstrated 3.6 m/s (8 mph).
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla Optimus: Recently reached a personal record of approximately 2.7 m/s (6 mph). RobotEra STAR1: Demonstrated speeds of 3.6 m/s (8.0 mph).

stories.headline: Unitree to Sell R1 Humanoid Robot Globally via AliExpress — First Marketplace Launch

key_facts.fact: Unitree Robotics will open sales of the R1 humanoid robot outside China via AliExpress next week, making it the first humanoid available for purchase on a general marketplace.
key_facts.excerpt: Unitree Robotics на следующей неделе открывает продажи робота R1 за пределами Китая — через AliExpress, сообщает Gizmochina. Это первый случай, когда гуманоидную машину можно будет заказать онлайн так же, как любой другой товар.

key_facts.fact: Sales will launch in North America, Europe, Japan, and Singapore; the R1 is 123 cm tall, weighs 27 kg, and sold in China from 29,900 yuan (~$4,100).
key_facts.excerpt: Старт охватит Северную Америку, Европу, Японию и Сингапур. Сам робот ростом 123 см и массой чуть более 27 кг. В Китае его выпустили в 2025 году по цене от 29 900 юаней.

key_facts.fact: Unitree shipped over 5,500 R1 units in 2025 — more than Tesla, Figure AI, and Agility Robotics combined (each shipped approximately 150 units).
key_facts.excerpt: В 2025 году Unitree отгрузила более 5 500 единиц R1 — больше, чем Tesla, Figure AI и Agility Robotics вместе взятые: каждая из этих компаний поставила примерно по 150 машин.

key_facts.fact: About 70% of R1 orders came from universities and research institutes; the company targets 10,000 to 20,000 units in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Около 70% заказов пришлось на университеты и научные институты. На 2026 год компания ставит цель — от 10 000 до 20 000 единиц.

key_facts.fact: Over 80% of R1 components are manufactured in China, giving Unitree a significant cost advantage over Western competitors whose humanoids cost up to $300,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Более 80% компонентов R1 производят внутри Китая. Для сравнения: аналогичные машины от западных производителей стоят до 300 000 долларов.

sources.title: На маркетплейсе можно будет купить гуманоидного робота Unitree

stories.headline: Anthropic Hires Microsoft AI Platform Lead Eric Boyd as Head of Infrastructure

key_facts.fact: Anthropic hired Eric Boyd from Microsoft to serve as Head of Infrastructure, overseeing the buildout of systems for its AI services.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has hired senior executive Eric Boyd from Microsoft to lead its infrastructure efforts, as the artificial intelligence company scales capacity to meet surging demand for its products. Boyd will serve as Head of Infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: At Microsoft, Boyd oversaw the company's AI platform and managed a team of approximately 1,500 employees.
key_facts.excerpt: Boyd brings deep experience from Microsoft, where he oversaw the company's AI platform and managed a team of approximately 1,500 employees.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has committed to spending $50 billion to build AI data centers in the United States.
key_facts.excerpt: The company previously committed to spending $50 billion to build AI data centers in the United States, positioning itself to handle what it has described as unprecedented demand.

key_facts.fact: The hire comes as Anthropic faces increasing usage of its models, including Claude Code, and has experienced occasional service disruptions tied to heavy usage.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has experienced occasional service disruptions tied to heavy usage, reinforcing the urgency of expanding its infrastructure footprint.

stories.headline: Generalist AI Unveils GEN-1 Robotics Model Claiming 99% Success on Physical Tasks

key_facts.fact: Generalist AI introduced GEN-1, an embodied foundation model that achieves 99% success rates on certain physical tasks, up from 64% for GEN-0, while completing tasks up to 3x faster.
key_facts.excerpt: GEN-1 achieves '99 percent success rates' on certain tasks, compared with around 64 percent for its previous-generation system, while completing tasks up to three times faster.

key_facts.fact: The company describes GEN-1 as 'the first general-purpose AI model that crosses a new performance threshold: mastery of simple physical tasks.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'We believe it to be the first general-purpose AI model that crosses a new performance threshold: mastery of simple physical tasks,' the company said.

key_facts.fact: GEN-1 requires roughly one hour of robot-specific data to adapt to new tasks, using large-scale pretraining on human activity data collected through wearable devices.
key_facts.excerpt: The system is also described as highly data-efficient, requiring roughly one hour of robot-specific data to adapt to new tasks. ... A key aspect of the approach is the use of large-scale pretraining on human activity data, collected through wearable devices.

key_facts.fact: Demonstrations showed robots performing tasks such as folding boxes, packing items, and assembling components over extended periods with hundreds or thousands of repetitions and minimal errors.
key_facts.excerpt: Demonstrations released alongside the announcement show robots performing repetitive tasks such as folding boxes, packing items and assembling components over extended periods without intervention.

sources.title: Generalist AI unveils GEN-1 model with 99% success in real-world robotic tasks

stories.headline: Analysts Say Google's TurboQuant LLM Compression Will Expand, Not Reduce, Memory Demand

key_facts.fact: Google's TurboQuant compression algorithm, detailed in March, can reduce KV cache memory usage by 6x and boost inference speed by 8x for large language models.
key_facts.excerpt: TurboQuant is a compression method that reduces the size of large language models (LLMs) with no loss of accuracy. It achieves this by shrinking the size of memory needed for training LLMs.

key_facts.fact: Despite initial fears that sent memory stocks lower, analysts and researchers now say TurboQuant is more likely to expand memory chip demand than reduce it — by removing bottlenecks, it enables training of bigger, more capable models.
key_facts.excerpt: Even if the technology proves successful in practice and enjoys widespread adoption, it will increase memory demand. Removing a bottleneck, such as huge memory requirements, can help AI companies train bigger, more capable models.

key_facts.fact: LLM parameter counts have grown from 0.09 billion in 2019 to over 1 trillion today; more efficient memory use historically drives demand for larger models rather than reducing total consumption.
key_facts.excerpt: The largest LLM in 2019 had just 0.09 billion parameters, a number that shot up to 540 billion in 2022. Unsurprisingly, the latest LLMs are being trained with more than 1 trillion parameters.

key_facts.fact: FT analysis cites experts concluding that more efficient AI could mean even greater need for semiconductors, reinforcing the Jevons paradox in AI compute.
key_facts.excerpt: More efficient artificial intelligence could mean even greater need for semiconductors, say experts.

key_facts.fact: Memory industry context: DRAM contract prices surged 55-60% QoQ in Q1 2026, with HBM now consuming 23% of total DRAM wafer output, up from 19% the prior year.
key_facts.excerpt: Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 55 to 60% quarter over quarter in Q1, while server DRAM surged more than 60%. HBM now consumes 23% of total DRAM wafer output, up from 19% the prior year.
